scope: PDF pages 191–351, second-half narrative and appendix; pages 352–390 are notes/index, used as finding aids.
attribution: All records paraphrase Carl Oglesby, The Yankee and Cowboy War. Interpretations and allegations remain attributed; this extraction does not independently confirm them. Citations are exact 1-based PDF file pages.

people.name: Chester Davis
people.description: Oglesby describes the lawyer defending Hughes in the TWA dispute and leading Toolco’s confrontation with Maheu.

people.name: Noah Dietrich
people.description: Oglesby describes the Toolco executive whose reduction of a credit request intensified a conflict with Hughes Aircraft managers.

people.name: John Sonnett
people.description: Oglesby describes the lawyer pursuing TWA’s antitrust case against Hughes, whose theory the Supreme Court ultimately rejected in the book’s account.

people.name: William O. Douglas
people.description: Oglesby describes the justice writing the majority decision assigning the Hughes dispute to aviation regulators.

people.name: Charles Metzner
people.description: Oglesby describes the judge presiding over damages proceedings in TWA v. Hughes.

people.name: Herbert Brownell
people.description: Oglesby describes the special master who reviewed depositions in the Hughes litigation.

people.name: Hank Greenspun
people.description: Oglesby describes a Maheu ally who stored the former Hughes aide’s document collection.

people.name: Jack Hooper
people.description: Oglesby describes the former FBI man running Hughes’s Nevada security force, left unaware of Hughes’s departure.

people.name: Paul Laxalt
people.description: Oglesby describes the governor praising Hughes’s economic importance and later speaking with a caller identified as Hughes.

people.name: Larry O’Brien
people.description: Oglesby describes the Kennedy associate whose firm accepted consulting work for Hughes; the author could not establish the full scope of that work.

people.name: Richard Danner
people.description: Oglesby describes a Nixon associate involved in the Hughes cash-transfer story and Maheu’s dismissal meeting.

people.name: John Meier
people.description: Oglesby describes the Nevada mining-claims adviser implicated in the book’s alleged silver-mining swindle; those allegations remain source claims.

people.name: Bill Gay
people.description: Oglesby describes the director who recruited Hughes’s personal aides and participated in the board’s moves against Maheu.

people.name: Howard Eckersley
people.description: Oglesby describes the aide said to have notarized the contested Hughes proxy and later delivered a supporting letter.

people.name: Levar B. Myler
people.description: Oglesby describes the aide who witnessed and stored the disputed proxy and later presented it to court.

people.name: James Golden
people.description: Oglesby describes a former Nixon Secret Service protector, Lockheed security executive and founding Intertel officer.

people.name: Edward P. Morgan
people.description: Oglesby describes Maheu’s lawyer and friend, involved in Hughes transfers and the formal dismissal meeting.

people.name: Robert Bennett
people.description: Oglesby describes the public-relations executive who brought the Toolco account to Mullen and convened discussion of Greenspun’s papers.

people.name: Ralph Winte
people.description: Oglesby describes the security successor with an Intertel background who met with Bennett and Hunt.

people.name: E. Howard Hunt
people.description: Oglesby describes the Watergate operative whose demands and wife’s death form the author’s account of the cover-up crisis.

people.name: G. Gordon Liddy
people.description: Oglesby describes the operative associated with the proposed Greenspun burglary and the Watergate entry team.

people.name: James W. McCord Jr.
people.description: Oglesby describes a former CIA security officer and CREEP security chief; the author hypothesizes a continuing covert CIA mission, which McCord denied.

people.name: Dorothy Hunt
people.description: Oglesby describes Howard Hunt’s wife, described as a contact for defendants’ financial support, killed aboard United Flight 553.

people.name: Gerald Alch
people.description: Oglesby describes McCord’s initial lawyer; he denied McCord’s claims that he proposed fabricating a CIA defense.

people.name: William Bittman
people.description: Oglesby describes the lawyer whose office Alch said he had visited before discussing trial silence with McCord.

people.name: Sherman Skolnick
people.description: Oglesby describes the investigator challenging the Flight 553 findings; the author acknowledges that his sabotage conclusions exceeded the evidence.

people.name: Alex Bottos
people.description: Oglesby describes a Sarelli-case informant whose claim connecting the crash with organized crime is recounted but not independently established.

people.name: John H. Reed
people.description: Oglesby describes the safety-board chairman asking the FBI to explain its early actions at the crash scene.

people.name: William D. Ruckelshaus
people.description: Oglesby describes the official responding that agents investigated possible federal violations and initially did not know Dorothy Hunt was aboard.

people.name: Egil Krogh
people.description: Oglesby describes the Special Investigative Unit organizer moved to the Department of Transportation after the crash.

people.name: Alexander Butterfield
people.role: White House aide and FAA administrator
people.description: Oglesby describes a Haldeman associate nominated to lead the FAA who later disclosed the White House recording system.

people.name: Dwight Chapin
people.description: Oglesby describes the Haldeman aide who later worked at United’s Chicago office and attended the Flight 553 hearings.

people.name: Richard Spears
people.description: Oglesby describes the political appointee whose changes in safety-board management were contested by C. O. Miller.

people.name: C. O. Miller
people.description: Oglesby describes the safety official challenging Spears’s asserted executive backing and interference in technical administration.

people.name: Ronald Dorfman
people.description: Oglesby describes the Chicago Journalism Review editor arguing against Skolnick’s poisoning inference.

people.name: Wendell Whitehouse
people.description: Oglesby describes the pilot whose toxicology and crash injuries are disputed in the book’s discussion of official findings.

people.name: Paul Gaynor
people.description: Oglesby describes the CIA contact who received McCord’s letters warning against attributing Watergate to the agency.

people.name: Jack Caulfield
people.description: Oglesby describes the intermediary accused in McCord’s account of offering clemency and receiving his Christmas warning letter.

people.name: Bernard Fensterwald
people.description: Oglesby describes the founder of the Committee to Investigate Assassinations and later McCord’s attorney.

people.name: Lou Russell
people.description: Oglesby describes the McCord employee and Fensterwald associate whose exchanged paychecks raised questions for the author.

people.name: Jimmy Carter
people.description: Oglesby describes the governor whose Trilateral membership and appointments the author interprets through his factional framework.

people.name: David Rockefeller
people.description: Oglesby describes the founder of the Trilateral Commission, in the book’s account, advised by Brzezinski.

people.name: Zbigniew Brzezinski
people.description: Oglesby describes the Trilateral adviser appointed Carter’s national security adviser.

people.name: Walter Mondale
people.description: Oglesby describes a Trilateral member selected as Carter’s running mate.

people.name: Cyrus Vance
people.description: Oglesby describes a Trilateral member appointed Carter’s Secretary of State.

people.name: Harold Brown
people.description: Oglesby describes a Trilateral member appointed Carter’s Secretary of Defense.

people.name: W. Michael Blumenthal
people.description: Oglesby describes a Trilateral member appointed Carter’s Treasury secretary.

people.name: Andrew Young
people.description: Oglesby describes a Trilateral member appointed Carter’s UN ambassador.

people.name: Richard Helms
people.description: Oglesby describes the agency director whom McCord admired and wrote to after Watergate; the author’s covert-direction theory is an inference.

people.name: Bernard Barker
people.description: Oglesby describes the entry-team member quoted about Dorothy Hunt’s funds and McCord’s decision to proceed.

people.name: John Sirica
people.description: Oglesby describes the judge receiving McCord’s March 19 letter.

organizations.name: Hughes Tool Company
organizations.description: In Oglesby’s account, the corporate board confronted Maheu over litigation and control of Nevada operations.

organizations.name: Hughes Aircraft Company
organizations.description: In Oglesby’s account, defense-oriented managers clashed with Toolco over borrowing and management autonomy.

organizations.name: Trans World Airlines
organizations.description: In Oglesby’s account, the airline disputed with Hughes over finance and antitrust jurisdiction.

organizations.name: Irving Trust
organizations.description: In Oglesby’s account, a TWA lender represented by Ben Sessel demanded a voting trust and loan terms.

organizations.name: Dillon, Read
organizations.description: In Oglesby’s account, the firm’s refinancing plan was central to Hughes’s loss-of-control dispute.

organizations.name: Desert Inn
organizations.description: In Oglesby’s account, the Las Vegas hotel-casino housed Hughes until his November 1970 departure.

organizations.name: Las Vegas Sun
organizations.description: In Oglesby’s account, Greenspun’s newspaper reported Hughes missing and its safe held Maheu’s papers.

organizations.name: Intertel
organizations.description: In Oglesby’s account, the security company, described as 94 percent owned by Resorts International, assisted Hughes’s Bahamas move.

organizations.name: Resorts International
organizations.description: In Oglesby’s account, the Bahamas casino operator competed with Hughes’s Nevada interests and owned most of Intertel.

organizations.name: Lockheed Aircraft Corporation
organizations.description: In Oglesby’s account, the aircraft company employed Golden and leased the JetStar used for Hughes’s departure.

organizations.name: Summa Corporation
organizations.description: In Oglesby’s account, the reorganized Hughes corporation succeeded the old Toolco structure.

organizations.name: Robert Mullen and Company
organizations.description: In Oglesby’s account, the PR firm maintained CIA cover relationships according to the Baker report cited by Oglesby.

organizations.name: Committee to Re-Elect the President
organizations.description: In Oglesby’s account, Nixon’s campaign committee employed McCord as security chief.

organizations.name: White House Special Investigative Unit (Plumbers)
organizations.description: In Oglesby’s account, the White House investigative group organized by Krogh is associated with burglary and political intelligence.

organizations.name: National Transportation Safety Board
organizations.description: In Oglesby’s account, the federal board investigated United Flight 553 and contested FBI and managerial actions.

organizations.name: Federal Aviation Administration
organizations.description: In Oglesby’s account, the aviation administration supplied crash evidence and was assigned to Butterfield.

organizations.name: Department of Transportation
organizations.description: In Oglesby’s account, the transportation department had overarching responsibility connected to the safety investigation.

organizations.name: United Air Lines
organizations.description: In Oglesby’s account, the Flight 553 operator employed Chapin in its Chicago market-planning office.

organizations.name: Bureau of Aviation Safety
organizations.description: In Oglesby’s account, the technical investigative unit led by Miller oversaw the crash inquiry.

organizations.name: Security International, Inc.
organizations.description: In Oglesby’s account, McCord’s private firm supplied security services and employed Russell.

organizations.name: Committee to Investigate Assassinations
organizations.description: In Oglesby’s account, Fensterwald’s small research organization collected information about JFK, RFK and King assassinations.

organizations.name: Trilateral Commission
organizations.description: In Oglesby’s account, the international policy group coordinated discussion among North America, Western Europe and Japan; the author interprets its influence as Yankee establishment power.

organizations.name: Democratic National Committee
organizations.description: In Oglesby’s account, the party headquarters was the target of the June 17 entry.

events.title: Hughes accepts TWA financing and voting trust
events.description: Oglesby describes Hughes accepting financing that left him without control; the account presents the terms as coercive.

events.title: Hughes divests TWA stock, in book’s dating
events.description: Oglesby describes the public sale of Hughes’s airline holding, handled by Merrill Lynch. This is the source’s date, retained without independent confirmation.

events.title: Hughes takes residence at Desert Inn
events.description: Oglesby describes Hughes arriving around Thanksgiving in a penthouse prepared by Maheu.

events.title: Maheu memo discusses hiring Kennedy aides
events.description: Oglesby describes a memo arranging O’Brien’s visit; the subsequent consulting contract is described but its full duties remain unclear.

events.title: Maheu receives authority over TWA litigation
events.description: Oglesby describes Hughes giving Maheu responsibility and the Toolco board confirming authority.

events.title: Metzner awards damages against Hughes
events.description: Oglesby describes a damages judgment exceeding $145 million, later increased with expenses and overturned.

events.title: Contested proxy grants Toolco authority
events.description: Oglesby describes a proxy said to be signed by Hughes, notarized by Eckersley and witnessed by Myler. The parties’ handwriting experts later disagreed.

events.title: Hughes leaves Las Vegas for Bahamas
events.description: Oglesby describes a secret departure via Nellis Air Force Base. The author interprets the board takeover as a coup; Nixon’s involvement is posed as a question.

events.title: Las Vegas Sun reports Hughes missing
events.description: Oglesby describes Greenspun’s headline after Maheu discovered Hughes had left.

events.title: Toolco formally dismisses Maheu
events.description: Oglesby describes Davis telling Morgan that Maheu was fired, citing the November proxy.

events.title: Proxy presented in control dispute
events.description: Oglesby describes Myler presenting the proxy to court and Eckersley bringing a purported Hughes letter; the court accepted Davis’s handwriting expert.

events.title: Meeting plans Greenspun document burglary
events.description: Oglesby describes a Mullen-office meeting determining on burglary, according to the testimony and reconstruction he cites; an April safe attempt was never conclusively linked to the Plumbers.

events.title: Entry team arrested at Watergate
events.description: Oglesby describes the taped-door sequence and arrest; his claim that McCord deliberately triggered discovery is an interpretation, denied by McCord.

events.title: McCord recounts Caulfield clemency offer
events.description: Oglesby describes McCord’s account of a meeting offering clemency and support, which he refused in conjunction with a CIA-blame strategy.

events.title: McCord writes Helms about CIA-blame narrative
events.description: Oglesby describes a letter alerting Helms to attempts to describe the break-in as a CIA operation.

events.title: McCord recounts trial-silence discussion
events.description: Oglesby describes McCord’s account of lunch with Alch about clemency, financial assistance and keeping defendants off the witness stand; Alch’s later denials are separately recorded.

events.title: United Flight 553 crashes at Chicago Midway
events.description: Oglesby describes the crash that killed Dorothy Hunt. The official account attributed the accident to crew handling; Skolnick and Bottos alleged sabotage, which the book does not establish.

events.title: Krogh moved to transportation department
events.description: Oglesby describes Krogh’s sudden DOT appointment, interpreted by Oglesby as potentially significant to the crash investigation.

events.title: Butterfield announced as FAA administrator
events.description: Oglesby describes the announcement followed by a delay until March because of restrictions on military officers holding the position.

events.title: McCord warns Gaynor about blaming CIA
events.description: Oglesby describes McCord’s letter advocating press leaks about pressure to blame the agency.

events.title: McCord discusses timing disclosures
events.description: Oglesby describes a further letter to Gaynor discussing holding evidence until the trial to maximize its effect.

events.title: Supreme Court reverses Hughes antitrust case
events.description: Oglesby describes the Court accepting Davis’s jurisdictional argument that the CAB, rather than the courts, had authority.

events.title: Flight 553 public hearings open
events.description: Oglesby describes the Chicago hearings attended by Chapin, amid disagreement over management of the investigation.

events.title: Skolnick seeks testimony at crash hearings
events.description: Oglesby describes Skolnick’s petition to inquiry chair Isobel Burgess, rejected in the author’s account.

events.title: Skolnick sues over crash hearings
events.description: Oglesby describes Skolnick filing a Cook County lawsuit against Burgess after describing the hearings as a sham.

events.title: Bottos detained for mental observation
events.description: Oglesby describes Bottos’s detention at Springfield; Bottos believed it prevented Sarelli testimony, while prosecutor Vaira later gave a different explanation for not calling him.

events.title: McCord sends letter to Judge Sirica
events.description: Oglesby describes the letter linking the Watergate operation to White House pressure and accelerating the crisis.

events.title: Krogh resigns DOT post
events.description: Oglesby describes Krogh’s resignation after his role in the Fielding burglary became public.

events.title: Alch denies proposed false CIA defense
events.description: Oglesby describes Alch’s testimony denying McCord’s accusations and asserting a prior McCord-Fensterwald connection.

events.title: IRS seeks Maheu material from Greenspun
events.description: Oglesby describes an IRS approach to Greenspun for the documents, blocked through court action in the author’s account.

events.title: NTSB asks FBI to explain early crash actions
events.description: Oglesby describes Reed’s letter asking why agents interviewed witnesses and heard tower tapes before safety investigators.

events.title: FBI explains response to Flight 553
events.description: Oglesby describes Ruckelshaus’s reply describing roughly fifty agents, first arrival within forty-five minutes, an investigation ending within twenty hours, and initial ignorance of Hunt’s presence.

events.title: NTSB issues final Flight 553 report
events.description: Oglesby describes the report and its crew-error reconstruction; the appendix challenges the spoiler explanation but does not establish an alternative cause.

events.title: Trilateral Commission formed
events.description: Oglesby describes Rockefeller creating the commission on Brzezinski’s advice; its relation to older networks is the author’s interpretation.

events.title: Maheu wins libel verdict
events.description: Oglesby describes a Los Angeles jury finding for Maheu after Hughes’s telephone accusations of dishonesty.

events.title: Carter appoints Trilateral members
events.description: Oglesby describes Carter’s selection of Vance, Brown, Brzezinski, Blumenthal and Young; the source’s explanation of factional influence remains an interpretation.

relationships.label: Employer and aide
relationships.description: Oglesby reports Hughes employing Maheu to manage Nevada operations and later assigning him litigation authority.

relationships.label: Rival authority claims
relationships.description: Oglesby reports Maheu and Davis disputing control of the TWA case and Nevada empire.

relationships.label: Document custodian
relationships.description: Oglesby reports Greenspun holding Maheu’s Hughes documents and tapes.

relationships.label: Majority ownership described
relationships.description: Oglesby reports Resorts International owning 94 percent of Intertel.

relationships.label: Cover relationship cited
relationships.description: Oglesby reports the Baker report describing CIA cover arrangements through Mullen.

relationships.label: Former security officer
relationships.description: Oglesby reports McCord’s official career in CIA security from 1951 to 1970.

relationships.label: Former special agent
relationships.description: Oglesby reports McCord’s FBI radio-intelligence and special-agent service.

relationships.label: Spouses
relationships.description: Oglesby reports Dorothy as E. Howard Hunt’s wife and a participant in financial-support arrangements.

relationships.label: Attorney-client relationship
relationships.description: Oglesby reports Alch representing McCord, followed by disputed accounts of defense strategy.

relationships.label: Later attorney-client relationship
relationships.description: Oglesby reports Fensterwald becoming McCord’s attorney after the Sirica letter.

relationships.label: Checks exchanged through CTIA
relationships.description: Oglesby reports Smith explaining that Fensterwald exchanged Russell’s McCord paychecks for personal checks; the author’s darker inference is unconfirmed.

relationships.label: Post-arrest correspondence
relationships.description: Oglesby reports McCord contacting Gaynor about CIA-blame narratives and timing disclosures.

relationships.label: Letter recipient
relationships.description: Oglesby reports McCord addressing a personal July 29 letter to Helms.

relationships.label: Clemency discussion and warning
relationships.description: Oglesby reports McCord recounting an offer of clemency and later writing Caulfield a warning.

relationships.label: Interagency correspondence
relationships.description: Oglesby reports Reed and Ruckelshaus exchanging letters about responsibility for the crash investigation.

relationships.label: Crash-investigation collaborators
relationships.description: Oglesby reports the two advancing a sabotage theory; their claims are not established by this extraction.

relationships.label: Disputed poisoning inference
relationships.description: Oglesby reports Dorfman arguing that Skolnick turned assumptions into conclusions on cyanide.

relationships.label: Safety-board management dispute
relationships.description: Oglesby reports Miller challenging Spears’s managerial authority and claimed external support.

relationships.label: Commission formation advice
relationships.description: Oglesby reports Rockefeller founding the commission on Brzezinski’s advice.

relationships.label: Presidential running mates
relationships.description: Oglesby reports Carter selecting fellow Trilateral member Mondale.

relationships.label: Author’s network interpretation
relationships.description: Oglesby reports Oglesby calling the commission an offshoot of the CFR and older networks; this is analytical linkage, not a verified legal affiliation.

relationships.label: Author’s network interpretation
relationships.description: Oglesby reports Oglesby tracing the commission to the Round Table tradition; no formal parent-body relation is established here.
